Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 76 s. 2021 JUN 15 2021 MS. ALELI MANIMTIM-CORDERO VP-Group Lega! Head Steel Corporation of the Philippines Philsteel Tower, 140 Amorsolo Street, Legazpi Village, Makati, Metro Manila Dear VP Cordero: This has reference to your letter dated 20 December 2019 requesting for this Department's assistance regarding the acts of the government the Provincial Treasurer, in relation to business related transactions in government. Per your letter, Steel Corporation (SCP) is a steel manufacturer with a plant in Balayan, Batangas, constructed from 1996 to 1998 and started commercial operations in 1999. In 1997, the machinery and equipment for the plant were purchased at time Of averaged PhP 26.30 per $1.00. Subsequently, on May 1999, after the machinery and equipment were installed, the Provincial Assessor of Batangas issued a real property tax assessment using the prevailing exchange rate at that time which was PhP 40.00 to $1.00. Due to the Provincial Assessor's continued refusal to revise the assessj-nent, SCP fiied a petition With the Locai Board Of Assessment Appeals (LBAA) while SCP paid real property taxes based on the adjusted value. On 02 February 2000. the DoF-BLGF issued a ruling sustaining SCP's position. However, the Provincial Assessor informed SCP that he was not in a position to implement the ruling of the DoF-BLGF in view of the pending petition with the LBAA. Instead, he advised SCP to withdraw the appeal to pave the way for the immediate implementation of the DOF-

BLGF opinion. Consequently, SCP withdrew its appeal with the LBAA However, the Provincial Assessor refused to implement the DoF-BLGF opinion which promted the SCP to again seek recourse from DoF-BLGF, which then issued an Indorsement dated 28 June 2000 stating that the considered resolved as it finds the defiance of the Provincial Assessor inaapropriate and without basis. However, despite this second disposition, the Provincial Assessor still refused to implement the DoF-BLGF opinion which impelled SCP to seek the assistance of then Department of Finance Secretary Camacho. On 22 Jnauary 2020, Secretary Camacho issued a ISt Indorsement confirming the 02 February 2000 DoF-BLGF opinion. Then on 05 April 2002, the BLGF Regional Director issued a 2nd Indorsement directing the Provincial Assessor to make the necessary correction in the assessment and instructed the Provincial Treasurer to recompute the real property tax liabilities of SCP based on the corrected assessrnents to ue by the rfOViflCia; Assessor. UnfOitunateiy, the Batangas Official refused to implement the DoF-BLGF opinion causing SCP to suffer arrearages as a result of the difference in the exchange rate used for determining acquisition cost and to make matters worse, then Governor Mandanas directed the iisuance of warrants of distraint and levy. In addition, Batangas Officials then proceeded to sell the properties at public auction and when SCP entered into a Memorandum of Agreement With the Of for the purpose Of its tax obligations, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan nullified the agreement, and the Provincial Treasurer directed the Municipal Treasurer to return the amount paid by SCP. As a consequence, SCP has been unable to secure a business permit, notwithstanding repeated efforts to pay and consign the taxes due. Then on 08 November 2019, the BLGF Executive Director issued a Memorandum to DOF Undersecretary Bayani H. Agabin, affirming its On 12 November 2019, SCP provided Engr. Eduardo B. Cedo, Provincial Assessor, a copy of Usec. Agabin's Indorsement. However, in his reply letter, the Provincial Assessor disregarded Usec. Agabin's indorsement. Under this premise arose the request for assistance regarding the acts of the government officials of Batangas, particularly the Provincial Assessor

and the Provincial Treasurer, in relation to business related transactions in government. At the outset, in as much as we would like to discuss the provisions of law 1 WI Wv Lu the in the letter, however, taking into account that the Department of Finance — Bureau of Local Government Finance (DoF-BLGF) have already issued an opinion regarding the matter, We deem it proper to defer to their position, considering that the issues contained herein squarely fall under their mandate and technical expertise. However, it is noteworthy to highlight that under our laws on taxation, in the appraisal of machinery and equipment for tax purposes, the rule is for the Sl we on its acquisition cost, using the prevailing exchange rate at the date of acquisition. Hence, this Department concurs with the DoF-BLGF opinion. At any rate, as to the acts of the government officials of Batangas, particularly the Provincial Assessor and the Provincial Treasurer, this Department deems it proper to stress that Republic Act No. 11032 (EODB Law), otherwise known as the "Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Delivery of Government Services Act of 2018", requires all local XL— a lillcu the issuance of business permits, clearance, and other types of authorizations, as well as set-up a one-stop-shop to facilitate all business transactions. Accordingly, this Department, together with the Department of Trade and Industry and Department of Information and Communication Technology, issued Joint Memorandum Circular (MC) 2016-01 or the Revised Standards in Processing Business Permits and Licenses in All Cities and Municipalities containing the guidelines in streamlining business permits and licensing system. Accordingly, the EODB Law Live CI 11 111 •a employees who may act inappropriately such as the refusal to accept application or request without due cause. Under the Manual on Real Property Appraisal and Assessment Operations, it states that any officer charged with the duty of assessing real property who intentionally violates or fails to perform any duty imposed upon him by law relating to the assessment of taxable real property shall be held liable. This includes any other officer required to perform acts relating to the administration of the rea: propel cy tax or to assist the assessor or treasurer in such administration, who willfully fails to discharge such duties.

Further, under Republic Act No. 6713, otherwise known as the "Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees", and the Rules Implementing the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees, it provides that public officials and employees shall, at all times, be accountable to the people and shall discharge their duties with utmost responsibility, integrity, competence, and loyalty, and uphold public interest over personal interest. In view of the foregoing, appropriate administrative proceedings may already be instituted or initiated against the Provincial Assessor and Provincial Treasurer, with the proper forum having jurisdiction over such government employees. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: RL L.
